# Queue Handoff

Durable work handoff via queue items. Lets the system keep moving
through compactions, missed messages, and interruptions by passing the
ball forward instead of leaving work suspended in chat or in-flight
without an owner.

## Use this when

- **Ending a turn on substantive work.** Active work should end by
  passing the ball to an owner or to the human — never by going idle
  with the rig appearing dormant.
- **Finishing a slice that has a clear next step.** Default-nudge:
  receiver gets a wake-ping plus the durable queue item.
- **Blocked on another agent's work.** Park the qitem with
  `closure_reason: blocked_on` and the blocker qitem id.
- **Escalating to the human.** Make the escalation a durable attention
  item, not just a chat message.

## Don't use this when

- The work is genuinely complete and there's no follow-on owner. Use
  `closure_reason: no-follow-on` (terminal completion) or
  `canceled`/`denied` as appropriate.
- The handoff would be too small and turn work into bureaucracy. Bundle
  the work into a coherent slice instead of decomposing every step.
- The handoff would be too broad and lose ownership/proof/closure
  criteria. Shape the qitem so the receiver knows the expected next
  action and closure evidence.

## The hot-potato terminal-turn-rule

Active work ends by passing the ball to a named next owner or to the
human. The qitem state machine enforces this:

`pending → in-progress → done` requires `closure_reason` from one of:

- `handed_off_to` — work continues at a different seat (target = new owner)
- `blocked_on` — parked pending another qitem (target = blocker qitem id)
- `denied` — receiver rejected the work
- `canceled` — sender or receiver withdrew
- `no-follow-on` — terminal completion, nothing else needed
- `escalation` — kicked up to a higher tier (target = escalation target)

Three of those (`handed_off_to`, `blocked_on`, `escalation`) additionally
require `closure_target`. The daemon enforces this at the domain layer;
every surface (CLI, MCP, future UI) inherits the same guarantee.

**The drafted-park failure (draft ≠ throw).** The rule is about the *actual* pass, not the
intention to pass. A turn that ends with a self-instruction **typed into your own prompt but left
unsent** — a drafted go-ahead, a next-atom note you never sent — has **not** handed off; it has
**parked**, and the seat sits idle for as long as nobody notices. Drafting the handoff feels like
doing it; it isn't. **Your last act on a turn must be an EDIT or a SEND** — a committed change, a
`rig send`, a `rig queue` handoff — **never a drafted prompt line left in the buffer.** If your
final output is an instruction addressed to yourself, you haven't ended the turn, you've stalled it.

**The dispatcher's other half — supersession closes your own outbox.** Ending your turn cleanly is
only half the rule; the other half fires when *you* move the world. **When a phase transition or a
fold receipt supersedes work you dispatched, close those dispatches yourself — with a citation to the
event that superseded them.** Closure-on-supersession belongs to the **dispatcher, never the
receiver.** Make it a habit: after every fold receipt / phase transition, run an **outbox audit** —
*which of my open dispatches did this just make moot?* — and close them with the citation.

*Why it must live with you:* stale dispatch-debt is **invisible to the dispatcher** because it lands
on someone else's queue — the cost is externalized, so no feedback loop ever fires to make you clean
it up. The receiver inherits debt they did not create and must burn cycles verifying it before they
can hold cleanly; a queue full of stale-pending makes *check-before-holding* — the discipline you
most want cheap — expensive, and it degrades the idle-detector's signal (a real owner looks the same
as a stale dispatch). Close it at the source: the moment your own transition mooted it.

**And after you hand off, PULL — don't idle with a stocked queue.** Handing the baton off ends the
*sequential* thread; it does not end *your* turn if your own queue still holds work. The circulation
pattern: finish → (1) hand the baton off so sequential work continues → (2) **check your OWN queue and
pull the next item** rather than going idle → (3) go truly idle only when your queue is **exhausted**,
then wait for the baton. An agent idling on top of a stocked queue is the single biggest utilization
leak (see `orchestration-team` → *queue depth is the orchestrator's product*). This is pull-not-push at
the seat level and needs no new machinery — the last act *after a handoff* is a **PULL**.

## Default-nudge semantics (the syntax footgun)

| Command | Nudges by default? | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `rig queue create` | yes | New qitem created from scratch |
| `rig queue handoff` | yes | Transactional close-as-handed-off + create-new |
| `rig queue handoff-and-complete` | yes | Atomic close + create-new; default nudge wakes the new owner |

**Footgun**: `--no-nudge` accidentally added to a live-loop handoff.
The shipped 0.3.1 CLI nudges by default on every queue write surface
(`rig queue create`, `rig queue handoff`, AND `rig queue handoff-and-complete`).
The only suppression flag is `--no-nudge` — appropriate for intentional
cold park, human-gate signal, or a deliberate poll-driven workflow, but
NOT for live-loop handoffs where motion matters.

**Rule**: in a live loop, omit `--no-nudge` and trust the default.
`--no-nudge` is the opt-out, not the opt-in. If you find yourself
reaching for `--notify`, stop — that flag does not exist on the
shipped 0.3.1 CLI; you may be following a stale instruction that
inverted the default-nudge polarity.

## Every queue row

- **`--summary "<what it is and why this seat>"`** on every `create`, `handoff` and `handoff-and-complete`: one or two plain sentences. It is the row's subject in RECENT, the story and the needs-you view, and a handoff does not inherit it from the source row.
- **Scope tags `project:<id>`, `mission:<id>`, `slice:<id>`** on project work, set when you create the row (`--tags`; `create` also takes `--mission` and `--slice`). Tags can't be edited afterwards. A handoff keeps the source row's tags unless you pass `--tags` or `--gate`, either of which replaces them; repeat the scope tags in `--tags` when you use `--gate`.
- **Pass work on with `handoff-and-complete`.** It closes your row as done and records the next row as its successor in one step. A `create` followed by `update --state done --closure-reason handed_off_to` records no successor, and the stuck sweep raises a recovery item for it.
- **Close what you hold.** A row you claimed ends in a handoff or an `update --state done --closure-reason …`; `rig queue overdue` lists claimed rows past their deadline.
- **Brief for the model that will read it.** Before handing a peer open-ended work, check which model it runs: `delegating-work`, "Check what kind of agent you're handing it to".

## Queue-body hygiene (token + parse safety)

The qitem body is durable DATA the daemon stores and replays on every
`rig queue show <id>` / `--json` read. Keep it small and parse-safe — a
bloated or malformed body costs every future reader, not just the
recipient.

- **No large command output in bodies.** Do NOT paste `rig ps`/`--nodes`
  dumps, big JSON blobs, full proof output, diffs, or transcript chunks
  into a qitem body. **Link the artifact PATH** (e.g.
  `missions/<m>/<slice>/proof.md`) or **summarize in prose**, then point
  at the file for the detail. A pasted dump makes `rig queue show <id>
  --full --json` large. Compact defaults limit a preview, but the stored body
  still costs readers who need full detail. Keep evidence in its durable artifact.
- **Substantive bodies go through `--body-file`, not inline `--body`.**
  For anything beyond a short line, write the body to a file and pass
  `--body-file <path>` (or `-` for stdin). Inline `--body` with shell
  metacharacters is fragile.
- **No raw backticks in bodies.** Backticks in an inline body are shell
  command-substitution and corrupt the payload (or execute). If you need
  code/command spans, use `--body-file`, or drop the backticks and write
  the command in plain text.

Heuristic: if the thing you want to include is more than a few lines or
contains shell metacharacters (backticks, `$`, quotes, newlines-with-pipes),
it belongs in a file you LINK, not in the body you paste.

The current `rig queue show` returns a bounded body preview by default;
`--full` returns the complete body and chain fields. Preview truncation does
not truncate the stored work. Check `bodyTruncated` and `bodyBytes`, then request
full content when needed; keep large supporting evidence in linked artifacts.

## Failure modes (6; verbatim)

1. Agent ends a turn without a handoff, so the rig appears idle.
2. Agent creates a queue item with `--no-nudge` inside a live loop, intending suppression of attention but breaking immediate motion. `--no-nudge` is for intentional cold park / human gate, not for routine live-loop handoffs. The opposite footgun — adding a `--notify` flag that does not exist on the shipped 0.3.1 CLI — comes from following stale instructions; the default already nudges.
3. Queue item is too small and turns work into bureaucracy.
4. Queue item is too broad and loses ownership, proof, or closure criteria.
5. Human escalation happens in chat but not as a durable attention item.
6. Agent pastes a large command dump (ps/nodes, big JSON, proof blob) into the qitem body, bloating the stored DATA so every full-body read is large. Link the proof PATH or summarize in prose; substantive bodies go through `--body-file`; no raw backticks inline.

## Durable handoff field shape

Every qitem carries:

- `handed_off_to` — destination session (qualified `pod-member@rig` form)
- `handed_off_from` — predecessor qitem id (the source session is `source_session`)
- `state` — one of: `pending | in-progress | done | blocked | failed | denied | canceled | handed-off`
- `closure_reason` + `closure_target` — set on terminal closure per hot-potato rule

**(0.5.0) `--body-context <ref>` — context riding the handoff.** `rig queue create … --body-context <ref>` attaches a composed context pack to the qitem. The snapshot rule: the qitem stores the **resolved content** in its body **plus the ref for provenance** — the handoff carries what was actually sent, and a later edit to the library never silently rewrites a past handoff's history. (The `rig context` noun composes the ref; the queue delivers it — the noun has no send.) See `openrig-user` → "Context packs and paced delivery."

The fields are auditable on the daemon-backed `rig queue` surface. Watchdog
policies and workflow runtime project new owners off these fields.

If a daemon-backed coordination command fails, debug the command/runtime/schema
edge directly — don't fall back to stale pre-upgrade assumptions.
"}}}

Usage: rig queue update [options] <qitemId>

Append a note and/or mutate qitem state. A note without --state never changes
row state. state=done REQUIRES --closure-reason (one of: handed_off_to,
blocked_on, denied, canceled, no-follow-on, escalation). Closure ≠ acceptance:
handed_off_to records delivery to the next stage; acceptance is the next stage's
verdict on its own qitem, not this closure.

Options:
  --actor <session>          (deprecated, ignored) the actor is derived from the
                             seat env (X-OpenRig-Session); P21 I3 made the
                             update route derive it from the transport header
  --state <state>            New state: pending | in-progress | done | blocked |
                             failed | denied | canceled | handed-off
  --reopen                   Explicitly acknowledge a deliberate
                             terminal-to-active repair; requires --state and
                             --note
  --closure-reason <reason>  Required for state=done; also 'superseded' on
                             state=canceled (with --closure-target = the
                             successor) records a supersession, distinct from an
                             abandoned cancel
  --closure-target <target>  Required for handed_off_to, blocked_on, escalation,
                             and superseded
  --resolution <text>        The outcome, stored on the row and shown by rig
                             queue show. Needs --state done, canceled, denied,
                             failed or handed-off, and non-blank text. Stored

                             the row already has (a fallback line, an earlier
                             outcome); a row that is already closed keeps what
                             it has
  --blocked-on <blocker>     For state=blocked: the blocker — a qitem id (must
                             exist and be live), a human seat (FR-6 park;
                             requires summary + evidence_ref), or a typed
                             non-qitem gate 'fold:<what>' / 'auth:<what>' /
                             'external:<what>'
  --wake-watchdog <jobId>    For state=blocked: attach an existing live watchdog
                             id targeting the row owner
  --wake-after <duration>    For state=blocked: atomically arm a timer (for
                             example 90s, 15m, 2h)
  --summary <text>           Summary persisted onto the item (human-seat parks,

  --evidence-ref <path>      OPR.0.4.4.19 FR-6: park-time durable-artifact

  --note <text>              Transition note for the audit log
  --full                     Print the whole response row(s) as today, even when
                             output.compact is on (the receipt's waiting keeps
                             only blocker and nextBackstop)
  --json                     JSON output for agents

# Glypherie review and correction loop

Configured for future assigned runs; execution is disabled and no run is instantiated. Native Codex owns authorized corrections. Actual Muse Spark 1.3 through Pi owns independent review. Read context.md and actual project AGENTS.md, then only task-relevant owner docs. Validation commands belong to justfile, lefthook.yml and component docs. Research, classification, revisions and optical acceptance belong to docs/evaluation.md and docs/revisions/README.md. Do not import Layout Editor validation conventions.

1. Operator records the user's objective, review/correction authority, intended base, branch, exact gate commands, owner/evidence destination, budget and stop condition in a copy of run-config.example.json. No inferred base from the currently checked-out branch. Resolve and record the merge-base. Default correction budget is three batches; workflow max_hops is twelve. Missing decisions block the run. Deliberately enable the config and validate the workflow before instantiation.
2. Capture complete branch diff from the selected merge-base plus staged, unstaged, deleted and untracked files, preserving owner edits. Use scenario.py snapshot CONFIG --tag UNIQUE. Helper records HEAD/index/base/branch and tracked/untracked content identity before and after. Drift blocks acceptance. Operational evidence must stay under .openrig. Never stash/reset/checkout user work.
3. Independent reviewer runs selected actual checks and classifies reproducible findings with IDs, paths/lines, effects, severity and evidence. Explicitly review implementation comments and reviewer comments. For geometric/model issues follow primary-source research before fixes, general invariants rather than per-glyph tuning. Mechanical tests do not establish optical acceptance; browser-based visual assessment must preserve the agreed preview and approved baseline.
4. Builder validates and deduplicates findings, records accepted/rejected/deferred reasons, groups accepted work into bounded tasks with exclusive file ownership, integration ownership and permitted concurrency. Delegate only when user scope explicitly authorizes it. Preserve unrelated work. Apply only authorized accepted corrections.
5. After EACH correction batch, perform the smallest appropriate affected checks and changed-file lint from repository owners. Immediately WRITE a summary of at most 150 words: changed behavior/files, actual checks/results, unresolved findings/gates and next owner. Keep detailed evidence separately linked. Review code comments and reviewer-comment dispositions for that batch.
6. Independent verification reopens actual implementation, tests, full selected-base plus dirty/untracked scope and all comments. scenario.py gates CONFIG --tag UNIQUE binds selected checks to candidate identity and supplies recorded BASE_REF/MERGE_BASE while preserving the environment. Drift makes successful commands stale. Required missing commands/services/providers are blocked, never a mock pass. Sonar is optional unless explicitly required for the run; if selected, actual scanner and quality-gate proof are both required.
7. Remaining correctable findings return to another bounded batch and summary, within budget. Close only with zero unresolved actionable findings and all assigned acceptance criteria/gates on the same candidate, including optical acceptance when required. Budget exhaustion, unavailable required provider/check or unknown optical outcome remains blocked/incomplete. No automatic commits, push, PR, publication or follow-on work.

Workflow mechanics: reviewer targets dev-review@glypherie without a harness pin because installed schema has no pi enum; builder pins codex. Exception owner operator-agent@kernel belongs to this separate instance. Use rig workflow project for atomic close/projection without duplicate dispatch. review hands findings to correct, correct hands off only after summary, verify failed loops to correct, verify clean hands to close, waiting records external blockers, done is reserved for actual closure.

Runtime binding directories remain ignored .openrig/seats. Actual project root /Users/dimitri/Documents/Code/personal/Inkplate/font_generator; .openrig/rig selects port7434 from outside seats. Read /Users/dimitri/.openrig-glypherie/topology/LEARNED.md and use existing Herdr provider only. Setup does not authorize any review or project checks.

  "name": "glypherie-review-correct",
  "project_root": "/Users/dimitri/Documents/Code/personal/Inkplate/font_generator",
  "execution_enabled": false,
  "base_ref": null,
  "branch": null,
  "evidence_dir": null,
  "max_correction_batches": 3,
  "validation_authority": "justfile, lefthook.yml and component docs selected through AGENTS.md",
  "record_authority": "docs/evaluation.md and docs/revisions/README.md; operational records under .openrig",
  "required_gates": [
    {
      "id": "focused-tests",
      "argv": null,
      "status": "select-per-authorized-run"
    },
    {
      "id": "changed-file-lint",
      "argv": null,
      "status": "select-per-authorized-run"
    }
  ],
  "aggregate_gate": "Select only task-required checks from repository authorities. No full build or optical publication implied.",
  "owners": {
    "builder": "dev-build@glypherie",
    "reviewer": "dev-review@glypherie"
  },
  "assignment_policy": "Per accepted finding, explicit exclusive paths, integration owner and allowed concurrency; preserve unrelated edits.",
  "evidence_dir_policy": "Operational outputs must resolve under project/.openrig; owner records require explicit authorized destinations.",
  "optional_analyzers": "SonarQube or other analyzers become required only when explicitly selected for the run; configure actual scanner and quality-gate commands. Missing a selected required analyzer is blocked."
}
workflow:
  id: glypherie-review-correct
  version: 1
  target:
    rig: glypherie
  objective: Follow /Users/dimitri/Documents/Code/personal/Inkplate/font_generator/.openrig/project/SCENARIO.md and the explicit per-run configuration supplied by the kernel operator. User objective, base selection, scope, correction authority, gates, canonical records and budget are required. This reusable spec is configured only; startup/setup does not authorize instantiation.
  loop_guards:
    max_hops: 12
  exception_routing:
    orchestrator_role: operator
  roles:
    operator:
      preferred_targets: [operator-agent@kernel]
    builder:
      preferred_targets: [dev-build@glypherie]
    reviewer:
      preferred_targets: [dev-review@glypherie]
  steps:
    - id: review
      actor_role: reviewer
      objective: Read actual project AGENTS and task-relevant research/evaluation/revision/component docs. Require an authorized per-run configuration and explicit base. Capture full committed plus staged/dirty/deleted/untracked scope from Git root, run configured required checks, independently review candidate and all code comments/review comments, and record reproducible findings in the assigned local operational records. No source edits. Handoff accepted findings to correct; missing gate/provider/base is blocked.
    - id: correct
      actor_role: builder
      harness: codex
      objective: Independently validate/dedupe reviewer findings, record all dispositions, and group bounded accepted tasks with exclusive file ownership. Implement only authorized accepted corrections, preserving concurrent edits. Choose affected tests/lint from justfile, lefthook.yml and component docs; no unselected aggregate gate. Inspect code and review comments. Immediately write a <=150-word batch summary of changed behavior/files, checks, unresolved work and next owner, with detailed evidence linked separately. Enforce per-run batch budget. Handoff to independent verification.
    - id: verify
      actor_role: reviewer
      objective: Reopen actual candidate, complete base plus dirty/untracked scope and every implementation/review comment. Independently verify corrections and required gates on matching candidate identity, including real Sonar quality-gate proof when selected by this scenario. Record remaining findings. Clean acceptance hands off to close; remaining correctable issues use failed to return to correct. Missing required gate/provider or exhausted budget is blocked/incomplete, never success.
      next_hop:
        on:
          failed: correct
    - id: close
      actor_role: builder
      harness: codex
      objective: Check zero actionable findings, all selected required gates and independent acceptance on the same candidate identity, summaries <=150 words for every batch, and explicit disposition of implementation and review comments. Record exact outcome and limitations in canonical records. Claim readiness only when the assigned required gates and any task-required optical acceptance passed. Use done only when assigned acceptance criteria settle; no commit/publication/follow-on without separate authorization.

import os, subprocess, shlex
pid=os.getpid()
for _ in range(7):
    raw=subprocess.check_output(['ps','-p',str(pid),'-o','ppid=','-o','comm=','-o','args='],text=True).strip()
    if not raw: break
    parts=raw.split(None,2)
    ppid=int(parts[0]); exe=parts[1]; argv=shlex.split(parts[2]) if len(parts)>2 else []
    flags=[]
    if 'codex' in exe.lower() or (argv and 'codex' in argv[0].lower()):
        for i,a in enumerate(argv):
            if a in ['--sandbox','--ask-for-approval','--add-dir','--cd','--model','-s','-a','-m']:
                flags.append([a,argv[i+1] if i+1<len(argv) else None])
            elif a in ['--full-auto','--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox']:
                flags.append([a])
    print({'pid':pid,'ppid':ppid,'executable':exe,'selected_codex_flags':flags})
    if ppid<=1: break
    pid=ppid
print({'session_env':{k:os.environ.get(k) for k in ['OPENRIG_SESSION_NAME','OPENRIG_HOME','OPENRIG_DAEMON_PORT','CODEX_THREAD_ID','CODEX_SANDBOX','CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED'] if k in os.environ}})
PY

# Evaluation principles for font fitting

## Research before implementation

Before tackling a problem or proposing a fix, search the project's papers and reference sources, reference
implementations and the web for existing solutions to that problem or its broader class. Prefer primary papers,
specifications and implementation sources. Check how each approach works, its assumptions and its applicability to the
project's constraints.

Present the best applicable approach to the user before implementation, with sources, the proposed adaptation, the
relationship it preserves and any limitations or departures from the original method. Prefer adapting an established
solution over inventing a new one.

Develop a new approach only as a last resort, after explaining why the researched solutions cannot reasonably be
adapted. Ground it in published principles, source geometry or established mechanisms; identify the novel part as a
project hypothesis and explain how it will be tested. A lack of a ready-made solution does not justify an unsupported
rule.

## Model and sources

Prefer a general, robust model with a clear geometric explanation. Begin with the feature being fitted, the source that
supports the approach and the geometric invariant it should preserve. Explain why the approach applies beyond the
reported glyph. Label project hypotheses explicitly and distinguish them from claims supported by the sources.

Every fitting decision, algorithm and logic change must have an external source foundation. An exception must be
explicitly specified and justified in both the code comment and the test; labelling a project hypothesis does not waive
this requirement. Compare implementation behavior with the cited sources and independently captured reference output.
Per-glyph or per-row rules need a computable, sourced geometric separator rather than isolated exceptions.

[Hersch 1993, sections 5–6](references/papers/1993-hersch/paper.md) explains how shape, placement on the pixel grid,
width relationships and continuity affect rendering. [Shamir 2003, section 3](references/papers/2003-shamir/paper.md)
grounds feature classification and preservation of geometric intent. Use these foundations to explain the model and
interpret its effects.

## Interpreting evidence

Judge changes against the source design. Do not optimize individual glyphs or rows for a tiny increase or decrease in
pixel count. Do not search for thresholds, phase choices, parameters or point exceptions to gain or remove pixels in a
reported glyph. Added ink can restore a stroke or damage a counter; removed ink can preserve contrast or disconnect a
join. Neither direction alone proves improvement or regression. Consider stroke weight, thick/thin contrast, joins,
counters, terminals and serifs together.

Hard contracts include determinism, required independent-reference parity, advances/layout, profile behavior, outline
validity and bounded movement/ownership. Mechanical checks establish comparable inputs and intact outputs. Preserving
geometric relationships and optical quality requires further judgment. Do not combine quality signals into an
unexplained acceptance score. Treat measurements as evidence to interpret:

- Point movement describes changes to corresponding endpoints and controls, not the distance between whole shapes.
  Interpret source-to-upstream, source-to-candidate and upstream-to-candidate changes separately, within each size.
- Connected ink and enclosed white regions need design context. A separate mark may be intentional; a new break may
  damage a join; a tiny counter may reasonably disappear at low resolution. Sensitivity to nearby coverage thresholds
  calls for investigation, while behavior across sizes, grid placements and axes needs broader evidence. Gray coverage
  samples describe hypothetical binary images rather than the delivered gray image.
- Ink area and feature counts describe activity, not quality. More detected or applied pairs can reflect broader
  coverage or mistaken classification. Check widths across source and fitted strokes, thick/thin contrast, fixed points,
  curve directions and which feature may move each point. A thin stroke gaining the weight of a thick stroke can lose
  intentional contrast despite gaining ink.

Favor tests of geometric relationships over a preferred pixel count. Include supported examples, transformed geometry
and cases where fitting should safely leave the source unchanged, especially joins, crossings, anchors, tangents and
conflicting point ownership. Compare source design and the independent reference across the agreed corpus and isolated
broader sweeps. Use exact pixels for an explicit identity contract, such as independent-reference parity or an untouched
rendering path.

Previously accepted glyphs may change during later model work. The user explicitly permits some rendering volatility:
acceptance describes the reviewed state rather than freezing its pixels or outline. Favor improvements to the general
model over preserving those snapshots, and do not add glyph exceptions or identity requirements to keep them fixed.
Assess subsequent changes for meaningful effects on source relationships and optical quality. Ordinary variation does
not automatically invalidate acceptance or require another review; a demonstrated defect or substantive unresolved
concern does. Record that concern and its inspection question in the affected iteration notes. Explicit contracts,
including disabled reference parity, untouched profiles and layout invariants, still apply.

## Review and decision

Classify findings by evidence rather than by difference from reference:

| Status               | Evidence                                                                                                                        | Required action                                                                      |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Confirmed regression | An explicit contract fails, or geometric/visual evidence demonstrates damaged stroke continuity, contrast, shape or legibility. | Fix the cause, or explicitly agree a limitation/follow-up.                           |
| Pending assessment   | A pixel, topology, width or size-transition difference raises concern, but damage has not been demonstrated.                    | Inspect source and fitted geometry, coverage and the web comparison before deciding. |
| Acceptable deviation | The output differs while preserving the intended relationships, and visual assessment supports the tradeoff.                    | Record the rationale and applicable scope; no compensating fix is required.          |

An increase in connected-component count establishes a change in a binary image. It does not locate the change or prove
that a principal stroke has broken: a small terminal, serif or marginal connection can change the count. A visible gap
damaging a source-connected stroke is stronger evidence than the count alone. Conversely, equal counts can hide damage.
Examine the location, geometric cause and behavior across relevant sizes/axes.

Conservative connectivity tests can pause a change for investigation without serving as an optical verdict. Historical
fixture names such as `known_join_failures` identify captured observations, not independently confirmed defects or
permission to accept them. Do not silently weaken a guard; an accepted deviation needs an explicit, recorded basis and
test expectations appropriate to that basis, without a glyph-specific production exception.

Use the current Rust evaluator and tests alongside the project's browser preview. Present glyphs and visual findings
through the browser app; do not present standalone images or local image links in chat. Only link rebuilt app content
reflecting the current changes. Explain model behavior and tradeoffs before interpreting pixel changes, and state
uncertainty and limitations. Select comparison inputs and preserve publication scope according to the
[generator contract](../tools/generator/CONTRACT.md#generation-selection). Passing mechanical checks alone does not
establish optical acceptance; closure follows the [iteration lifecycle](revisions/README.md#iteration-lifecycle).

## Review questions and findings

Classification is part of the agent's work on every batch, not a deterministic rendering or evaluation algorithm. Before
requesting review, identify what actually changed in the relevant source feature against the selected baseline and
record the evidence in the iteration notes. Choose the inspection question from that assessment:

- Thinning: inspect continuity and retained shape, especially joins and terminals.
- Thickening: inspect optical weight and balance against neighboring strokes.
- Mixed thinning/thickening: inspect both affected roles and retained contrast; a single net ink change hides this case.
- Shape or placement changes: inspect the affected curve, alignment or attachment.
- Unchanged output: distinguish an existing reported concern from a change introduced by this batch.

These are judgment categories, not automatic sign tests or an exhaustive fixed taxonomy. Local taper/placement changes
and rounding can differ from the main stroke intervention. Explain those distinctions rather than deriving a verdict or
review group from a scalar measurement. Rendering and evaluation tools must not assign semantic classifications.
Reassess findings when subsequent fitting changes invalidate their descriptions.

Check the final published output for the reviewed profile as well as the outline. When geometric or coverage changes
produce an identical final bitmap, describe the visible concern as unchanged output; record the geometric intervention
separately in the iteration notes. Do not imply visible thinning or thickening from subpixel outline movement alone.

Record unresolved findings in the affected iteration before requesting visual assessment. Identify family, symbol, size,
axes and output profile, the inspection question, evidence and disposition. Keep unassessed cases pending; accepted
deviations need a rationale and scope. Passing tests alone does not resolve a finding. Findings must not become fitting
exceptions. Broader diagnostic findings stay in iteration notes and isolated output until a publication-scope change is
agreed.

## Usage

Run from the repository root:

```sh
mkdir -p out/diagnostics
cargo run --locked --manifest-path tools/generator/Cargo.toml \
  --bin font_evaluate -- tools/generator/specimens.json out/diagnostics/evaluation.json
```

The command evaluates the configuration's latest selected variant across its existing size/axis/profile matrix,
comparing independent source without hinting, independent upstream hinting and the candidate. It writes JSON; preview
publication is separate and the matrix stays unchanged.

A hard check failure writes JSON and returns a nonzero exit status. Input or capture errors abort the run. Diagnostics
alone leave the exit status successful. Read the report alongside geometric tests and the web preview; a successful run
confirms mechanical checks, not optical acceptance.
# Development revisions

Revisions group iterations; each iteration groups related topics for review: corrections, improvements, capabilities or
investigations.

## Folder structure

- `README.md`: this guide.
- `NNN/README.md`: revision starting point, renderer identities and iteration index with brief outcomes or status.
- `NNN/NN-topic.md`: iteration design and decision note; for example, `001/02-light-continuity.md` is iteration 001.02.

## Iteration documents

Write a design and decision note, grouping topics by a shared goal, model or invariant rather than by glyph or work
step:

- **Title and introduction:** motivation and adopted approach.
- **Foundation and invariant:** shared sources and preserved relationships. Follow the
  [evaluation rules](../evaluation.md); label project hypotheses. Put distinct foundations beside their topics.
- **Topics:** one subsection per topic, numbered when useful, explaining the logic change and rationale. Retain rejected
  alternatives only when they explain a decision or constraint.
- **Scope and limits:** applicability, accepted review scope, limitations and unresolved work or assigned follow-up.
  Keep essential assessment evidence beside the relevant topic or limitation.

Describe the resulting behavior, not its implementation, testing or publication history. Replace superseded proposals;
omit file maps, handoffs, command/build logs, verification ledgers and artifact metadata. Keep detailed diagnostics
elsewhere. Avoid repeated status, unchanged-state reminders and document-routing prose; unchanged behavior matters only
as an invariant or scope boundary.

## Documentation ownership

The revision index owns lifecycle status, closure dates and renderer identities; iteration notes own model decisions and
scoped assessment. Evaluation principles belong in the [evaluation guide](../evaluation.md); commands, APIs and
interface contracts belong in tool documentation. Preview selections belong in configuration and policy files. Link to
the owner rather than repeat its content. Vendored baseline/candidate documentation remains independent.

## Iteration lifecycle

Feedback may extend an iteration's agreed topics. Close only with explicit user agreement and a disposition for each:
completed, accepted with limits, declined or deferred to a specific follow-up. Passing tests, publishing a preview or
completing one topic does not close the group. Advance numbering after closure, with the next scope agreed from
feedback.

default:
    @just --list

# Install commit tooling and activate the Git hooks in this clone.
hooks-setup:
    git lfs install --local
    mise install --locked dprint just lefthook node npm:cspell
    mise exec -- npm ci --ignore-scripts
    mise exec -- lefthook install

# Check a commit message file, defaulting to the most recent message.
commit-check message_file=".git/COMMIT_EDITMSG":
    mise exec -- node node_modules/@commitlint/cli/cli.js --edit "{{message_file}}"

# Validate a range of new commits.
commit-check-range from to="HEAD":
    mise exec -- node node_modules/@commitlint/cli/cli.js --from "{{from}}" --to "{{to}}" --verbose

# Test the hook and commit-message validation behavior.
hooks-test:
    mise exec -- npm test

# Check Rust formatting without changing files.
rust-fmt-check:
    cargo fmt --manifest-path tools/generator/Cargo.toml --check

# Install the pinned formatter and spell checker using mise.
docs-setup:
    mise install --locked dprint node npm:cspell
    mise exec -- dprint resolved-config > /dev/null

# Format Markdown prose, tables, and JSON files.
fmt:
    mise exec -- dprint fmt

# Check Markdown and JSON formatting without changing files.
fmt-check:
    mise exec -- dprint check

# Check spelling in the project documentation.
spell-check:
    mise exec -- cspell --no-progress --gitignore

# Install the pinned web runtime and locked web dependencies.
web-setup:
    mise -C tools/web install --locked node
    mise -C tools/web exec -- npm ci --ignore-scripts

# Build the WASM font renderer via tools/wasm/build.sh (owned separately; never
# installs toolchains). The browser app stages the source package into a
# hashed Vite asset; inputs are documented in the [WASM interface](tools/wasm/README.md).
wasm-build:
    tools/wasm/build.sh web

# Build the candidate-enabled preview WASM renderer. Uses the opt-in `preview`
# cargo feature, which enables the generator's `candidate` feature; the output
# (tools/wasm/pkg-web-preview-simd128/) uses standard SIMD and stays separate
# from the production artifact (tools/wasm/pkg-web/, built by `wasm-build`).
wasm-build-preview:
    WASM_SIMD128=1 tools/wasm/build.sh web preview

# Build the browser app into out/web/.
web:
    npm --prefix tools/web run build

# Serve the browser app with live reload, without generating specimens.
dev $web_port="8903":
    npm --prefix tools/web run dev -- --port="$web_port"

# Serve the current browser app; `preview` keeps the review-workflow name.
alias preview := dev

# Serve the built app separately from the dev server.
web-serve:
    npm --prefix tools/web run preview

# Generate and publish the configured specimen packages.
specimens $config_path="tools/generator/specimens.json" $output_dir="out/specimens":
    cargo run --locked --manifest-path tools/generator/Cargo.toml --bin font_specimens -- "$config_path" "$output_dir"

# Check web browser types without emitting files.
web-typecheck:
    mise -C tools/web exec -- npm run typecheck

# Run the web tests with the pinned runtime.
web-test:
    mise -C tools/web exec -- npm test

# Serve isolated web components with live reload.
web-storybook:
    mise -C tools/web exec -- npm run storybook

# Build the component explorer into out/storybook/.
web-storybook-build:
    mise -C tools/web exec -- npm run build-storybook

# Export aligned glyph images and pixel differences from published renders.
comparisons $config_path="tools/generator/comparisons.json" $specimen_dir="out/specimens":
    cargo run --locked --manifest-path tools/generator/Cargo.toml --bin font_comparison -- "$config_path" "$specimen_dir"

# Stage Playdate Font Lab and compile out/playdate-font-lab/FontLab.pdx.
playdate-build *args:
    node tools/playdate/build.mjs {{args}}

# Build FontLab.pdx and open it in the SDK Simulator.
playdate-run *args:
    node tools/playdate/build.mjs --run {{args}}
lefthook: mise exec -- lefthook
glob_matcher: doublestar

pre-commit:
  parallel: true
  jobs:
    - name: formatting
      glob: "**/*.{md,json,jsonc}"
      exclude:
        - "docs/references/VisualTrueType/**"
        - "docs/references/specs/**"
        - "**/vendor/**"
        - "**/package-lock.json"
        - "**/.mise/**"
        - "**/node_modules/**"
        - "**/target/**"
        - "**/out/**"
        - "**/.venv/**"
      run: mise exec -- dprint check {staged_files}
    - name: spelling
      glob:
        - "README.md"
        - "AGENTS.md"
        - "fonts/**/*.md"
        - "docs/**/*.md"
        - "tools/**/*.md"
        - "experiments/**/*.md"
      exclude:
        - "docs/references/VisualTrueType/**"
        - "docs/references/specs/**"
        - "docs/references/papers/*/paper.md"
        - "**/vendor/**"
        - "**/node_modules/**"
        - "**/target/**"
        - "**/out/**"
        - "**/.venv/**"
      run: mise exec -- cspell --no-progress --gitignore --no-must-find-files {staged_files}
    - name: rust-formatting
      glob:
        - "tools/generator/**/*.rs"
        - "tools/generator/Cargo.toml"
      exclude: "tools/generator/vendor/**"
      run: cargo fmt --manifest-path tools/generator/Cargo.toml --check

commit-msg:
  jobs:
    - name: conventional-commit

wasm-build-preview:
    WASM_SIMD128=1 tools/wasm/build.sh web preview

# Build the browser app into out/web/.
web:
    npm --prefix tools/web run build

# Serve the browser app with live reload, without generating specimens.
dev $web_port="8903":
    npm --prefix tools/web run dev -- --port="$web_port"

# Serve the current browser app; `preview` keeps the review-workflow name.
alias preview := dev

# Serve the built app separately from the dev server.
web-serve:
    npm --prefix tools/web run preview

# Generate and publish the configured specimen packages.
specimens $config_path="tools/generator/specimens.json" $output_dir="out/specimens":
    cargo run --locked --manifest-path tools/generator/Cargo.toml --bin font_specimens -- "$config_path" "$output_dir"

# Check web browser types without emitting files.
web-typecheck:
    mise -C tools/web exec -- npm run typecheck

# Run the web tests with the pinned runtime.
web-test:
    mise -C tools/web exec -- npm test

# Serve isolated web components with live reload.
web-storybook:
    mise -C tools/web exec -- npm run storybook

# Build the component explorer into out/storybook/.
web-storybook-build:
    mise -C tools/web exec -- npm run build-storybook

# Export aligned glyph images and pixel differences from published renders.
comparisons $config_path="tools/generator/comparisons.json" $specimen_dir="out/specimens":
    cargo run --locked --manifest-path tools/generator/Cargo.toml --bin font_comparison -- "$config_path" "$specimen_dir"

# Stage Playdate Font Lab and compile out/playdate-font-lab/FontLab.pdx.
playdate-build *args:
    node tools/playdate/build.mjs {{args}}

# Build FontLab.pdx and open it in the SDK Simulator.
playdate-run *args:
    node tools/playdate/build.mjs --run {{args}}
lefthook: mise exec -- lefthook
glob_matcher: doublestar

  parallel: true
  jobs:
    - name: formatting
      glob: "**/*.{md,json,jsonc}"
      exclude:
        - "docs/references/VisualTrueType/**"
        - "docs/references/specs/**"
        - "**/vendor/**"
        - "**/package-lock.json"
        - "**/.mise/**"
        - "**/node_modules/**"
        - "**/target/**"
        - "**/out/**"

        - "tools/**/*.md"

commit-msg:
